articles.title: 两度摘得诺奖的女人

core_fact_map.core_fact: 华沙大学不接纳女性；玛丽1891巴黎求学；与皮埃尔结婚合作。

source_evidence.english: Marie Curie was born Maria Skłodowska on 7 November 1867 in Warsaw, then under Russian dominion, where women were denied university admission.
source_evidence.chinese: 玛丽·居里原名玛丽亚·斯克沃多夫斯卡，1867年11月7日生于华沙。当时华沙处于俄国的统治(dominion)之下，在那里，女性被剥夺了(were denied)大学的入学资格(admission)。

source_evidence.english: Eager to pursue formal study, she emigrated to Paris in 1891, enrolling at the Sorbonne.
source_evidence.chinese: 渴望(Eager)追求(pursue)正规的(formal)学习，她于1891年移居(emigrated)巴黎，注册入读(enrolling)索邦大学。

source_evidence.english: On 26 July 1895 she wed the physicist Pierre Curie, forging a research partnership.
source_evidence.chinese: 1895年7月26日，她与物理学家皮埃尔·居里成婚(wed)，两人建立起(forging)研究上的合作关系(partnership)。

core_fact_map.core_fact: 贝克勒尔先发现铀发射射线；玛丽命名放射性；居里夫妇发现钋和镭，成吨矿石提得约0.1克氯化镭。

source_evidence.english: Henri Becquerel found that uranium emitted rays; she named this property of certain elements radioactivity.
source_evidence.chinese: 亨利·贝克勒尔发现，铀会发出射线(rays)；她把某些元素(elements)的这种性质/属性(property)命名为放射性(radioactivity)。

source_evidence.english: In July 1898 the Curies announced polonium, a tribute to her motherland, and on 26 December, radium.
source_evidence.chinese: 1898年7月，居里夫妇宣布发现了钋，以此致敬(tribute to)她的祖国(motherland)；12月26日，他们又宣布发现了镭(radium)。

source_evidence.english: In a leaky shed they painstakingly processed tonnes of pitchblende, a uranium ore; by 1902 she had recovered about a tenth of a gram of radium chloride.
source_evidence.chinese: 在一间漏雨的(leaky)棚屋里，他们费尽心力地(painstakingly)处理了成吨(tonnes)的沥青铀矿，这是一种铀矿石(ore)。到1902年，她已提取(recovered)出约十分之一克(gram)的氯化(chloride)镭。

core_fact_map.core_fact: 1903三人共享物理学奖；玛丽是首位女性诺奖得主；提名遗漏由皮埃尔坚持纠正。

source_evidence.english: On 10 December 1903 she jointly won the physics Nobel with Pierre and Becquerel, the first woman so recognised.
source_evidence.chinese: 1903年12月10日，她与皮埃尔和贝克勒尔共同(jointly)获得诺贝尔物理学奖，第一位获此认可的(recognised)女性。

source_evidence.english: The nomination had initially left her out; at Pierre's insistence, the omission was rectified.
source_evidence.chinese: 提名最初(initially)把(left out)她排除在外了(left out)；在皮埃尔的坚持(insistence)下，这一疏漏(omission)得到了纠正(rectified)。

core_fact_map.core_fact: 皮埃尔遇难、玛丽继任女教授；1911顶住私生活风波独获化学奖；两门科学获奖的独特性。

source_evidence.english: On 19 April 1906 a horse-drawn wagon fatally struck Pierre.
source_evidence.chinese: 1906年4月19日，一辆马拉的货车(wagon)致命地(fatally)撞上了皮埃尔。

source_evidence.english: On 5 November she gave her inaugural lecture as his successor, the Sorbonne's first woman professor.
source_evidence.chinese: 11月5日，她作为他的继任者(successor)发表了就职(inaugural)演讲，成为索邦大学第一位女教授。

source_evidence.english: In November 1911 a press scandal about her private life erupted; she was urged to stay away.
source_evidence.chinese: 1911年11月，一场关于她私生活的媒体丑闻(scandal)爆发(erupted)，有人劝她不要前往。

source_evidence.english: Undeterred, she collected the chemistry Nobel, won outright, on 10 December.
source_evidence.chinese: 她并没有被吓住(Undeterred)，于12月10日，领取了完全(outright)属于她的诺贝尔化学奖。

source_evidence.english: Her distinction in two sciences remains unmatched.
source_evidence.chinese: 她在两门科学中双双获得诺贝尔奖，这份荣誉(distinction)至今仍无人企及(unmatched)。

core_fact_map.core_fact: 一战X光设施服务逾百万伤员；1934血液病死因很可能关联长期辐射；遗留笔记仍有放射性。

source_evidence.english: In the First World War she mobilised X-ray vans and stationary posts that examined over a million casualties.
source_evidence.chinese: 第一次世界大战期间，她动员/调用了(mobilised)X光面包车(vans)和固定(stationary)站点，这些设施检查了超过一百万伤亡人员(casualties)。

source_evidence.english: She died on 4 July 1934 of a blood disorder, probably caused by prolonged exposure to radiation.
source_evidence.chinese: 1934年7月4日，她死于一种血液疾病(disorder)，这很可能是由长期(prolonged)暴露于辐射所导致的。

source_evidence.english: Her notebooks, still radioactive, are preserved in lead-lined boxes at the National Library of France; readers sign a liability waiver and don protective garments.
source_evidence.chinese: 她的笔记本至今仍有放射性(radioactive)，保存(preserved)在法国国家图书馆的铅(lead)衬的盒子里；读者须签署免责协议(liability waiver)，并穿上(don)防护(protective)服装(garments)。

source_evidence.english: The pages retain her handwriting and her radium.
source_evidence.chinese: 这些书页留存(retain)着她的笔迹(handwriting)，同样也留存着她所发现的镭。

changes.reason: 首奖三名获奖者和提名遗漏/纠正是人物归功与女性受阻的关键链。

articles.title: 微塑料：无处不在，危害几何？

core_fact_map.core_fact: 2004存档海洋样本显示微小塑料碎片与合成纤维增多；微塑料一词由此提出。

source_evidence.english: In May 2004 Richard Thompson, a marine biologist at the University of Plymouth, and colleagues described an overlooked pollutant in the journal Science.
source_evidence.chinese: 2004年5月，理查德·汤普森，一位海洋的(marine)生物学家(biologist)，任职于普利茅斯大学，在《科学》杂志上，他和同事们描述了一种被忽视的污染物(pollutant)。

source_evidence.english: Sifting through plankton samples kept since the 1960s, they found that microscopic plastic fragments and synthetic fibres had grown more abundant.
source_evidence.chinese: 细细筛查(Sifting through)自20世纪60年代起保存下来的浮游生物(plankton)样本，他们发现，极其微小的(microscopic)塑料碎片(fragments)和合成(synthetic)纤维(fibres)变得越来越多(abundant)。

source_evidence.english: They labelled the particles microplastics.
source_evidence.chinese: 他们把(labelled)这些颗粒(particles)称为(labelled)微塑料。

core_fact_map.core_fact: 环境广布；美国2015立法监管微珠先于人体危害获证。

source_evidence.english: Since then the durable debris has proved ubiquitous, turning up on shorelines, in deep-sea sediment, in rainfall, and in Arctic ice.
source_evidence.chinese: 此后，这些经久不烂的(durable)碎屑(debris)被证明无所不在(ubiquitous)，出现(turning up)在海岸线(shorelines)上、深海沉积物(sediment)里、雨水(rainfall)中，以及北极的冰层中。

source_evidence.english: Regulation came before proof of harm to people: in December 2015 America passed a law banning plastic microbeads from scrubs and other cosmetics rinsed down drains.
source_evidence.chinese: 监管(Regulation)先于人体受害的证据出现：2015年12月，美国通过了一项法律(passed a law)，禁止把塑料微珠用在磨砂膏(scrubs)等化妆品(cosmetics)里，这类产品用后会被冲进(rinsed down)下水道。

core_fact_map.core_fact: 22名健康献血者约四分之三检出血中塑料；另项颈部动脉斑块研究只发现风险相关，不能证明因果。

source_evidence.english: The search turned inward.
source_evidence.chinese: 人们的搜寻随后转向了体内(turned inward)。

source_evidence.english: In March 2022 a small Dutch study found plastic in the blood of about three-quarters of 22 healthy donors.
source_evidence.chinese: 2022年3月，一项小规模的荷兰研究发现，22名健康献血者(donors)中，约四分之三的人血液里有塑料。

source_evidence.english: In March 2024 a study in the New England Journal of Medicine linked plastic in the fatty plaque of neck arteries to a higher risk of heart attack, stroke, or death.
source_evidence.chinese: 2024年3月，《新英格兰医学杂志》上的一项研究，将颈部动脉(arteries)脂肪性(fatty)斑块(plaque)中的塑料，与心脏病发作、中风(stroke)或死亡的更高风险联系了起来。

source_evidence.english: Its authors cautioned that correlation is not causation.
source_evidence.chinese: 该研究的作者警告(cautioned)称，相关性(correlation)并不等于因果关系(causation)。

core_fact_map.core_fact: 信用卡摄入量估算被批高估；脑内一勺是大众转述，脑组织研究方法受质疑。

source_evidence.english: The most sensational figures are the shakiest.
source_evidence.chinese: 最耸人听闻的(sensational)数字，就是最不可靠的(shakiest)。

source_evidence.english: In June 2019 a report for WWF, a conservation group, reckoned people might swallow a credit card's worth of plastic a week; critics call that an overestimate.
source_evidence.chinese: 2019年6月，一份和自然保护(conservation)组织 WWF 有关的报告估算(reckoned)，人们每周可能吞下(swallow)相当于一张信用卡分量的塑料；批评者称其高估了(overestimate)。

source_evidence.english: In February 2025 a study in Nature Medicine reported plastic in brain tissue in an amount popularised as a spoonful; others queried its methodology.
source_evidence.chinese: 2025年2月，《自然·医学》上的一项研究报告了脑组织(tissue)中的塑料，其含量被大众传作“一勺(spoonful)”；其他人则质疑了(queried)其研究方法(methodology)。

core_fact_map.core_fact: WHO2019判断仅限饮水当时含量且证据有限；检出与相关尚未确定人体危害。

source_evidence.english: Two months later the World Health Organization was reassuring but tentative: on limited evidence, microplastics in drinking water posed no apparent risk at current levels.
source_evidence.chinese: 两个月后，世界卫生组织的表态令人安心(reassuring)，但只是试探性的(tentative)：基于有限的证据，饮用水中的微塑料，按照当前的含量，并未构成明显(apparent)风险。

source_evidence.english: Detection has outrun understanding; human studies remain small or observational.
source_evidence.chinese: 检测(Detection)走在了认识前面；针对人体的研究仍然规模较小，或只是观察性的(observational)。

source_evidence.english: Harm is plausible but unproven, and until the verdict is in, better measurement may guide policy more safely than panic.
source_evidence.chinese: 说它有害合乎情理(plausible)，却尚未证实(unproven)；而在定论(verdict)出来之前，依据更好的测量(measurement)来指导政策，或许会更稳妥，胜过任由恐慌(panic)左右。

articles.title: OK 原本是个玩笑

core_fact_map.core_fact: 1838报纸错拼缩写风潮；1839已有已知最早o.k.。

source_evidence.english: OK, often said to be the planet's most frequently spoken word, began as a newspaper gag.
source_evidence.chinese: OK，常被说成是全世界最常(most frequently)说出的词，起初只是报纸上的一个噱头(gag)。

source_evidence.english: From 1838 abbreviations were all the vogue in Boston's papers, and the craze turned comic through deliberate misspellings: O.W. for 'oll wright', K.Y. for 'know yuse'.
source_evidence.chinese: 从1838年起，缩写(abbreviations)风靡(all the vogue)于波士顿各大报纸，而且这股狂热(craze)也变得滑稽(comic)起来，通过故意的(deliberate)错误拼写(misspellings)：用 O.W. 代表 'oll wright'，用 K.Y. 代表 'know yuse'。

source_evidence.english: The humour lay in the persona of an uneducated bumpkin.
source_evidence.chinese: 幽默(humour)在于(lay in)一个没受过教育的(uneducated)乡巴佬(bumpkin)人物角色(persona)。

source_evidence.english: On 23 March 1839 a Boston Morning Post satire took a swipe at a contemporary, the Providence Journal, over a mock society parodying an ordinance against ringing dinner bells.
source_evidence.chinese: 1839年3月23日，《波士顿晨邮报》的一篇讽刺文章(satire)抨击了(took a swipe at)一个同时期的(contemporary)报纸《普罗维登斯日报》，话题是一个恶搞的(mock)社团，它戏仿(parodying)一项禁止敲开饭铃的法令(ordinance)。

source_evidence.english: It carried the first known 'o.k.', glossed as 'all correct'.
source_evidence.chinese: 它刊载了已知最早的“o.k.”，被注释为(glossed as)“all correct”（完全正确）。

core_fact_map.core_fact: oll korrect是all correct的故意错拼；缩写的幽默来自模仿文盲口吻。

source_evidence.english: The humour lay in the persona of an uneducated bumpkin.
source_evidence.chinese: 幽默(humour)在于(lay in)一个没受过教育的(uneducated)乡巴佬(bumpkin)人物角色(persona)。

source_evidence.english: The letters stood for a knowingly illiterate 'oll korrect'.
source_evidence.chinese: 这两个字母代表的是有意(knowingly)写成文盲(illiterate)拼法的'oll korrect'。

core_fact_map.core_fact: 1840范布伦绰号Old Kinderhook也为OK；竞选阵营借双关传播。

source_evidence.english: Partisan politics propagated the letters nationwide.
source_evidence.chinese: 党派(Partisan)政治在全国宣传了(propagated)这些字母。

source_evidence.english: In 1840 Martin Van Buren, the incumbent president, sought re-election.
source_evidence.chinese: 1840年，在任(incumbent)总统马丁·范布伦寻求连任(re-election)。

source_evidence.english: His New York backers, punning on his nickname 'Old Kinderhook', after his birthplace, formed the Democratic O.K. Club, making the letters a double-meaning slogan.
source_evidence.chinese: 他在纽约的拥护者(backers)拿(punning on)他的绰号 'Old Kinderhook' 玩双关(punning on)，这个绰号得名于他的出生地(birthplace)，他们成立了民主党 O.K. 俱乐部，让这两个字母成了一句一语双关的(double-meaning)口号(slogan)。

core_fact_map.core_fact: 范布伦败选、OK留存；杰克逊批注传闻属捏造，约20年内真实正式用法才普及。

articles.title: 改变世界的科学巨匠

core_fact_map.core_fact: 1919日食结果被当时机构誉为支持太阳引力使星光偏折，爱因斯坦成名。

source_evidence.english: On 29 May 1919, as a total eclipse obscured the sun, two British expeditions photographed stars in its apparent vicinity.
source_evidence.chinese: 1919年5月29日，一次全日食(eclipse)遮蔽了(obscured)太阳，两支英国考察队(expeditions)拍摄了天空中看似位于太阳附近(vicinity)的恒星。

source_evidence.english: Arthur Eddington observed from Príncipe, an island off West Africa; Crommelin and Davidson from Sobral, in north-eastern Brazil.
source_evidence.chinese: 阿瑟·爱丁顿观测(observed)于普林西比岛，这是一座岛，位于西非外海；克罗姆林和戴维森则在索布拉尔，位于巴西东北部。

source_evidence.english: They were testing general relativity's bold prediction that the sun's gravity would deflect starlight.
source_evidence.chinese: 他们要检验广义相对论(general relativity)的一个大胆的(bold)预言，也就是太阳的引力(gravity)会使经过它附近的星光偏折(deflect)。

source_evidence.english: On 6 November, at a joint meeting of the Royal Society and the Royal Astronomical Society, the findings were hailed as confirming it.
source_evidence.chinese: 11月6日，英国皇家学会与皇家天文学会召开联席(joint)会议，观测结果(findings)被盛赞为(hailed as)证实了这一预言。

source_evidence.english: The Times proclaimed a "Revolution in Science"; a New York Times headline read "Lights All Askew in the Heavens".
source_evidence.chinese: 《泰晤士报》宣告了(proclaimed)一场“科学革命”；《纽约时报》的标题(headline)写着“天上的光全歪了”。

source_evidence.english: Almost overnight, Einstein, eminent among physicists, became a global celebrity.
source_evidence.chinese: 几乎一夜之间(overnight)，在物理学家(physicists)中卓越的(eminent)爱因斯坦成了举世皆知的名人(celebrity)。

core_fact_map.core_fact: 一位委员判断相对论实证不足；全奖1921因无提名满足标准而依章程保留。

source_evidence.english: Stockholm proved harder to dazzle.
source_evidence.chinese: 斯德哥尔摩却没那么容易被眩惑(dazzle)。

source_evidence.english: The Nobel physics committee valued rigorous experimental confirmation, and committee member Allvar Gullstrand, a Nobel-winning eye specialist, deemed the empirical support for relativity insufficient.
source_evidence.chinese: 诺贝尔物理学委员会看重的是严格的(rigorous)实验(experimental)证实(confirmation)，而委员会(committee)成员阿尔瓦·古尔斯特兰德，一位获得过诺贝尔奖的眼科专家(specialist)，认定(deemed)相对论的实证(empirical)支持不足(insufficient)。

source_evidence.english: Since no nomination fulfilled Nobel's criteria, the 1921 prize was reserved for a year, as the statutes permit.
source_evidence.chinese: 由于没有一项提名(nomination)符合(fulfilled)诺贝尔定下的标准(criteria)，1921年的奖被保留(reserved)一年，这是章程(statutes)所允许(permit)的。

core_fact_map.core_fact: 1922授的是保留的1921奖，给爱因斯坦理论物理贡献，尤其光电定律。

source_evidence.english: On 9 November 1922 the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences conferred it on Einstein, citing his services to theoretical physics, especially his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect.
source_evidence.chinese: 1922年11月9日，瑞典皇家科学院把这个奖授予(conferred on)爱因斯坦，表彰(citing)他对理论物理学的贡献，尤其是他发现了光电效应定律。

core_fact_map.core_fact: 光电作用是光使金属释放电子，定律助量子理论；授奖决定次日的信件明确该奖不考虑相对论。

source_evidence.english: That law, which governs how light ejects electrons from metal, helped underpin quantum theory.
source_evidence.chinese: 这条定律决定了(governs)光如何把电子(electrons)从金属中打出(ejects)，曾帮助奠定(underpin)量子(quantum)理论的基础。

source_evidence.english: A letter the next day clarified that the prize took no account of relativity.
source_evidence.chinese: 第二天的一封信澄清(clarified)，此奖并未考虑(took no account of)相对论。

core_fact_map.core_fact: 赴日未到典礼；1923诺奖演讲专谈未被奖项考虑的相对论，构成故事反讽。

source_evidence.english: Einstein, then aboard a steamer bound for Japan, would miss the December ceremony.
source_evidence.chinese: 爱因斯坦当时正乘(aboard)一艘开往(bound for)日本的轮船(steamer)，将错过12月的颁奖典礼(ceremony)。

source_evidence.english: On 11 July 1923, in Gothenburg, Sweden, he delivered his Nobel lecture before a congress of Nordic scientists, devoting it to the fundamental ideas and problems of relativity.
source_evidence.chinese: 1923年7月11日，在瑞典哥德堡，他发表了(delivered)他的诺贝尔演讲(lecture)，面向北欧自然科学家大会(congress)，专门(devoting to)讲相对论的基本(fundamental)思想与问题。

source_evidence.english: The theory the committee looked past reached a Nobel podium after all, carried there by the man the prize had honoured.
source_evidence.chinese: 委员会绕开不看的那个理论，终究登上了诺贝尔的讲台(podium)，把它带上去的，正是这个奖所嘉奖(honoured)的爱因斯坦。
